  "text": "The footsteps in the hall reached the front door. Its latch clicked, though no one had lifted the bar.

At the kitchen threshold, a voice said, “Mara.”

Venn’s wife tightened her grip on Ada’s hand. The constable stood a few paces away, staring at the dark marks gathering beneath the rain barrel.

“Mara,” the voice said again. It was Venn’s voice, but he had never called his wife by her given name where anyone could hear.

The front door opened. A second voice, farther away, called, “Don’t answer him.”

Elias came into the yard and shut the kitchen door behind him. “There’s no one in the hall,” he whispered.

Something struck the door at the height of its handle. The constable backed away. His torn sleeve, still in Ada’s hand, began to pull toward the house.

Mara held the heated key against the sleeve’s stitches. They parted one by one. Inside the cuff lay a narrow strip of paper, rolled so tightly that Ada had to use her nails to open it.

Three names were written there: ELIAS, ADA, MARA. Beneath them was a blank line.

From the front of the house came Venn’s cry. “It’s asking for a fourth.”

The kitchen door rattled. The marks under the barrel spread into tiny fingers and gripped the constable’s boots.

Mara took the paper from Ada. With the key’s hot tip, she wrote VENN on the empty line.

The fingers released the constable. Inside, both sets of footsteps ran for the cellar."
